entry.title: Fix-It Felix Jr has now arrived on the Amiga and it looks really good!
entry.content:
The classic arcade vibe of Wreck-It Ralph which leapt off the cinema screen on to the Commodore 64, and then on to the ZX Spectrum Next, has now arrived on the Commodore Amiga thanks to BrokenBytes. While fans have spent years recreating the movie's fictional 1982 arcade hit Fix-It Felix Jr. on everything from mobile phones to the ZX Spectrum, a definitive new version has appeared as a port to the Commodore Amiga. While Steven Day recently reached out to us to share this exciting news, you can check out the latest screenshots and details below.

ZX Spectrum Next - Amiga Gameplay Soon!

The game faithfully reimagines the chaotic story of Ralph raging against the Nicelanders who bulldozed his forest home to build an apartment complex. Players step into the shoes of the town's brave handyman, Felix Jr., scaling the building to repair every broken window with his father's magic golden hammer while avoiding falling bricks thrown by Ralph and passing ducks. To survive the timer across each floor, players can grab piping-hot apple pies left on window sills by grateful residents, granting Felix temporary invincibility, brick-smashing power, and scoring multipliers.

This new Amiga version delivers an incredibly authentic arcade experience. The release boasts striking PAL OCS graphics, fluid hardware animations, fully animated cinematic cutscenes—including the iconic rooftop victory celebration, smooth building scrolling and moving clouds, original artwork, sampled sound effects and speech, three-channel music and so much more. So yes, an incredible release and worthy of a big feature on IndieRetroNews.

Credits

  • Amiga conversion: Antonio Savona (Broken Bytes)
  • Graphics & visual art: Steven Day
  • Music & sound design: Aldo Chiummo
  • Original score & tunes: Saul Cross
  • Original concept & lore: Tobikomi Company / Walt Disney Animation Studios
  • (C) 1982, 2026 Tobikomi / Broken Bytes. All rights reserved.

entry.title: Enhanced framerate versions of Amiga games via AI and Vesuri
entry.content:
Vesuri with the help of AI is aiming to give many classic Amiga games a bit of a performance boost and some much needed bug fixes. For some time now, Amiga owners have faced a frustrating bottleneck: purchasing powerful hardware expansions—like the legendary Apollo 1240 accelerator card for the Amiga 1200—only to find that most classic games still struggled to run smoothly. Because early 90s software was rarely written for these faster, upgraded hardware setups, even the most expensive configurations left players disappointed. Drawing on extensive expertise from the Amiga demo scene, Vesuri recognized that the hardware was capable of far more, sparking a long-held ambition to patch these foundational software limitations to make the most out of powerful accelerators.

▶ Ver vídeo en YouTube

The breakthrough arrived after Vesuri successfully optimized the classic Stunt Car Racer to run at a blistering 50 frames per second. While that initial project required painstaking manual programming, recent technological leaps in artificial intelligence opened the door to a much faster, more scalable approach. By combining advanced AI tools with an intimate knowledge of the Amiga’s custom architecture, Vesuri is now actively releasing enhanced frame-rate versions of highly requested games on GitHub. These upgrades build directly upon existing WHDLoad infrastructure established by scene veterans like JOTD, Psygore, StingRay, and CFou!. To keep the installation process simple and avoid disrupting upstream maintainers, players can easily upgrade their experience by swapping out the original slave files, bringing enhanced performance updates to old classics. To see what's current being worked on with the latest video's it's worth visiting the website link all the way at the bottom.

▶ Ver vídeo en YouTube

Wing Commander Amiga Enhanced

  • Optional enhanced framerate with smoother flight, cameras and ship effects.
  • Consistent game speed on faster processors and smoother cinematic movement.
  • Retimed intro, room, briefing, launch, landing, death and funeral animations.
  • Improved projectile appearance and asteroid/mine hit detection.
  • Waypoint markers stay visible in front of nebulae in every English mode.
  • More responsive room controls with limited cursor speed.
  • Disk edition: faster arithmetic and collision checks in every mode, including the Amiga 500, without changing game behaviour.
  • Enhanced mode and caches enabled in newly installed icons; original modes remain available.

▶ Ver vídeo en YouTube

Their Finest Hour Enhanced

  • Enhanced framerate: faster, tear-free rendering and full ground detail on fast Amigas, with consistent game speed at different frame rates
  • Corrected controls, aiming, bullet hits, bombing, AI and gameplay timing with Enhanced framerate enabled
  • Adjustable mouse sensitivity: 1x, 2x (default), 4x or 8x
  • Improved flight recording and playback, with 128-second recordings
  • Fixed repeating explosion and splash sounds
  • Enhanced framerate is enabled in the supplied game icons (CUSTOM2=1). Uncheck it in the WHDLoad startup options to use the original game mode
  • New enhanced movie saves require Enhanced framerate in this slave; original movie files can still be loaded

▶ Ver vídeo en YouTube

Road Rash Enhanced

  • Enhanced framerate for smoother, vsynced play on Fast RAM Amigas, enabled in the installed icon (CUSTOM2=1)
  • consistent simulation speed on the accelerated path, with reduced visible steering lag and corrected opponent lane occupancy
  • fixed distant and mirror bike flicker and vertical jumps on hills
  • fixed joystick steering recentring and keyboard/CD32 pause handling
  • fixed a loading crash on uncached 68030 machines
  • blanked the border during play on ECS/AGA machines
  • updated installer; cancelling replacement preserves an existing installation

▶ Ver vídeo en YouTube

Red Baron Enhanced

  • CPU-specific rendering improvements and consistent game speed under one Enhanced framerate checkbox, enabled in the supplied icons.
  • ReadMe and installer adapted to the WHDLoad Install Template, retaining JOTD's three-disk layout, executable decompression and icon choices.

▶ Ver vídeo en YouTube

Test Drive Enhanced 

  • Optional Enhanced framerate for smoother driving, scenery and traffic, with more consistent race timing and average-speed scoring.
  • Fixed sideways road and scenery jumps, including through bends.
  • Restored steering response through bends.
  • Fixed nearby vehicles disappearing before a collision.
  • Fixed the rev counter needle wrapping around when over-revving.
  • Fixed repeated drum hits in the opening music.
  • Improved compatibility with accelerated Amigas.
  • Updated installer and clearer setup instructions.

▶ Ver vídeo en YouTube

4D Sports Driving Enhanced

  • Fixed the flickering blue background in the DSI intro.
  • Faster rendering with a single "Enhanced framerate" option, enabled in the installed icon (CUSTOM2=1).

entry.title: The Curse of Sherwood - Sunteam remakes a classic Mastertronic title for the PC!
entry.content:
Sunteam is back with some 8-bit nostalgia with their latest PC remake, The Curse of Sherwood. This latest release modernises a classic budget arcade adventure originally crafted by Derek Brewster and published by Mastertronic back in 1987 for the ZX Spectrum, Commodore 64, and Amstrad CPC. Heavily inspired by the iconic Spectrum edition, the game plunges players into an endangered Sherwood Forest, which has fallen under the tyrannical control of the sinister Cult of Sagalia. After Robin Hood and his Merry Men suffer a devastating defeat at the hands of the cult, a desperate Friar Tuck seeks the aid of the Bishop of Derby to perform a grand exorcism. However, the plan takes a dark turn when the Bishop is found dead, leaving behind a bloody parchment inscribed with a cryptic rhyme that holds the ultimate secret to destroying the cult once and for all.


▶ Ver vídeo en YouTube

Stepping into the sandals of Friar Tuck, players must navigate a treacherous, flick-screen world viewed from an elevated side angle to locate the artifacts necessary to complete the holy mission. Strategy is key, as Tuck's inventory is strictly limited to carrying just three items at a time, forcing players to think carefully about where and when to deploy their findings across the dense forest layout. The woodland paths are teeming with hostile creatures that will fire projectiles at any opportunity, and a single touch from these enemies or their weapons will cost you one of your three precious lives. Fortunately, the holy man isn't entirely defenseless; you can retaliate by throwing swords and gradually upgrading your arsenal to more powerful weaponry as you explore deeper into this charmingly reimagined retro quest from Sunteam.

AI Assisted, Sounds

  • We sourced music from Pixabay but did not realise that the tune used AI until it was near release and by then it just fitted the game so well that we decided not to change it. In future we will be more vigilant and do our best to source only human made audio.

entry.title: Ash - A lovely looking Amiga platformer based on the Norwegian folk tales of Askeladden is teased [UPDATE]
entry.content:
Welcome to Ash, an ambitious new platformer currently in development for the Commodore Amiga by Thomas Mayer Foss. The game draws deep inspiration from Norwegian folklore, centering on the traditional tales of Askeladden. Players will guide the underestimated youngest brother on a grand quest to win a princess and half a kingdom. To overcome the game's various obstacles, players can dynamically swap between three unique companions met along the way: the Stone Eater, the Light-Footed One, and the One of Thirteen Winters and Seven Summers, each possessing distinct abilities essential for progression. The adventure will span five beautifully detailed worlds, guiding players from dense forests and rugged mountains up into the clouds, ultimately leading to a final showdown at the king's court and the mountain troll's lair.


▶ Ver vídeo en YouTube

Built as a passionate hobby project with a commitment to completion, Foss is designing the game specifically to push original hardware limitations without any AI graphics. The custom game engine is written entirely in Assembler code to deliver rich graphics, complex mechanics, and true parallax scrolling on a standard Amiga 500 OCS with just 512KB chip RAM and 512KB slow RAM. Early gameplay footage showcasing the vibrant forest world confirms the title runs at a smooth 50 frames per second on real hardware. While the game's soundtrack remains a work in progress, Amiga gamers can follow regular devlogs, concept art updates, and full world previews directly on the official project page, Ash - a game for Amiga.

[UPDATE] A demo has been released with the following being said "  This is an early prototype. The level in this build is a test playground for showing off features, not a real level from the game. Expect rough edges, placeholder content and lots of changes. "

entry.title: Time Pilot - Konami's 1982 Arcade game has been ported over to the Amiga
entry.content:
Even more Amiga news for you today as RMJ and JoeJoe, has released a 1:1 conversion of Konami’s 1982 classic Time Pilot to the Amiga 500 and 1200. Rather than a standard emulation or loose recreation, this involved translating the original arcade machine's Z80 processor instructions entirely into 68000 assembly code, instruction by instruction. Furthermore, this conversion replicates the intense aerial combat of the multidirectional shooter, where players pilot a jet through an indefinitely scrolling open airspace. Each distinct stage shifts the battlefield to a completely different historical time period, staying completely faithful to the legendary arcade game originally distributed by Centuri and Atari.

▶ Ver vídeo en YouTube

According to the wiki page "this game originally dominated arcades before seeing early home ports on systems like the Atari 2600, MSX, and ColecoVision in 1983. While Konami would later pivot the series with a top-down arcade sequel in 1984, Time Pilot '84, that follow-up completely abandoned the signature time-travel theme in favour of a purely futuristic backdrop." By focusing strictly on the charm of the 1982 original, RMJ and JoeJoe have delivered a rather decent retro preservation project that gives both standard OCS Amiga 500 users and AGA Amiga 1200 owners a way to experience one of gaming's foundational arcade shooters.

  • Although the website description does look as if it was done by AI, there's no mention if the game was developed with the help of AI either on the page or as a disclaimer. So make of that as you will.

entry.title: Pinball Illusions – The Vikings table arrives on the Amiga AGA via PC {AI WIP}
entry.content:
Well, here's some interesting news for the weekend, as the elusive fourth table, The Vikings, is unofficially making its way to the Amiga A1200 (AGA). While the original 1995 release of Pinball Illusions famously included only three tables on the Amiga, the PC version was fortunate enough to receive the Norse-themed addition. Now, thanks to a dedicated developer by the name of MrDig, with the help of Claude AI to migrate the PC data, the table is being converted to run natively on the original Amiga engine. The port integrates into the classic menu as a proper fourth selection, complete with its own dedicated high-score list, menu picture, and custom info text.

▶ Ver vídeo en YouTube

The project has already achieved a small milestone, with full gameplay proving highly stable on both physical A1200 hardware and the FS-UAE emulator. Packed using Imploder to save valuable chip RAM, the conversion successfully runs all core mechanics, including the dot-matrix ship mini-game, Thor and Labrador multiballs, and end-of-ball bonuses. While the table is fully playable via hard-disk installation and WHDLoad, the developer is currently polishing the remaining animations, synchronising the audio with the PC original, and exploring an optional feature to centre the game screen on modern monitors.

  • Via the sourced linked forum thread you will find table4 bin files you can place in the WHDLoad version "PinballIllusions v2.2 AGA". See the readme.txt for instructions. Expect bugs, and do report them (preferably screenshots/videos of the bugs) so I can feed those to claude and make it better.

entry.title: Amiga 1942 - The Amiga gets a smooth scrolling Arcade port from retrodnagames!
entry.content:
Well, here's a Sunday surprise! As Retrodnagames has released a fan-made port of Capcom’s legendary 1984 arcade shooter 1942! This impressive homebrew project brings the classic vertical shoot-'em-up to the Commodore Amiga with an uncompromising, old-school ethos. Retrodnagames has coded the entire game from the ground up using AsmOne assembly language, painstakingly rebuilding all 32 stages, enemy flight patterns, and maps from scratch simply by studying arcade gameplay videos. Proudly crafted entirely by hand without any AI assistance, the port achieves decent performance too, boasting vibrant 32-colour graphics that run at a silky-smooth 50 frames per second at a native 224x256 resolution.

▶ Ver vídeo en YouTube

This ambitious release aims to honor the legacy of the original arcade smash hit designed by Yoshiki Okamoto, which originally served as the foundational entry in Capcom's iconic 194X franchise. Set in the Pacific Theater of World War II and loosely based on the historic Battle of Midway, the game uniquely tasks players with fighting their way to Tokyo to dismantle the enemy air fleet—a design choice originally tailored to capture Western markets that helped the game become a massive global financial success in the mid-1980s (wiki). This definitive Amiga tribute includes every single enemy type from the original cabinets, all the classic power-ups, and there's even a few hidden surprises!

Minimum System requirements:

  • OCS PAL Amiga. Runs on ECS and AGA as well
  • Floppy version: 512K chip mem, and 512K any mem
  • HD version: 512K chip mem, and 1Mb any mem. WHDLoad 17+

entry.title: Amiga Outrun AGA - Retrodnagames works his magic on a classic Arcade racer for the Amiga!
entry.content:
The Amiga news is coming in thick and fast, as now we welcome the release of 'Outrun AGA', an ambitious fan-made reimagining of Sega’s legendary arcade racer built to replace the notoriously poor official Amiga port from back in the day. Developed by retrodnagames, this project is coded entirely from the ground up in old-school assembly language. Steering clear of modern shortcuts, the developer proudly avoided any form of generative AI during creation to hopefully ensure an authentic arcade experience. Built to squeeze every ounce of power from original, 1993-era Commodore hardware, the racing title is purely blitter-driven, requiring a PAL-based AGA Amiga equipped with a standard 68020 CPU and 4MB of fast RAM. Because of its specialized reliance on native Amiga custom chips, faster modern processor upgrades won't alter the game's execution speed.

▶ Ver vídeo en YouTube

Outrun Amiga, Yeh it's that bad!


▶ Ver vídeo en YouTube

Amiga Outrun AGA - Music seems a little glitchy, may be emulator related!


This impressive technical feat perfectly honours the spirit of Yu Suzuki's iconic 1986 masterpiece. This native Amiga recreation packs in all 15 stages bringing the complete journey to life in a crisp 320x224 fullscreen resolution. Visually anchored by a striking 32-colour display mode running at a steady 25 frames per second, the game delivers beautiful sprite-scaling action that mirrors the coin-op original. Players can cruise to all three original music tracks while simultaneously listening to robust three-channel sound effects, keeping the immersive premium stereo experience intact. Best of all, Amiga owners can lock in their best runs with high scores saved directly to a hard drive across every distinct difficulty setting.


Minimum System requirements:


  • AGA PAL Amiga with 4Mb fast RAM. Runs full speed on 68020. This is intended to run on close to original 1993 C= hardware. Since the game is blitter driven, faster CPU's will not make it run faster.

entry.title: Wipeout 2097/XL - A Playstation hit futuristic racer gets an Amiga AI port, albeit beefy Amiga's required!
entry.content:
Welcome to Wipeout 2097/XL, a native AmigaOS 3 port rebuilt entirely from a source decompilation of the original PlayStation code. Coded by Arcziii (arczi84) with the help of AI, this non-commercial port relies on modern hardware expansions, requiring an Amiga system running PiStorm with a Raspberry Pi 3, 4, or CM4 under Emu68. To handle the high-octane 3D performance, your setup must feature RTG with a 32-bit screen mode, roughly 64 MB of free RAM, and an active AHI sound subsystem. Players can choose between two specialized render versions depending on their software setup: xl-ogles using the ogles2.library with MSAA support, or xl-minigl utilising minigl.library v29. Performance tests show that the MiniGL build provides an extra boost, clocking in at roughly 10 frames per second faster. 

▶ Ver vídeo en YouTube

If you've got the power, then this release offers Amiga owners the definitive way to experience one of the greatest video games of all time. Centered around the iconic F5000 AG racing league, the game challenges players to pilot blazing-fast, weapon-equipped futuristic crafts across gravity-defying global race tracks. Wipeout originally defined mid-90s gaming culture, praised heavily by critics for its distinct visual aesthetic, alongside its ground breaking licensed soundtracks featuring artists like The Chemical Brothers and The Prodigy. Wipeout 2097 even received critical acclaim upon release; reviewers praised the game for its dramatic improvements to the controls, graphics, and gameplay of the original Wipeout (Wiki).

  • You will need to provide your own original Wipeout XL USA PlayStation retail disc (SCUS-94351) or a corresponding digital .bin/.cue image, as the download contains no copyrighted game data. Helpfully, the package does include NR74W's beautiful HD texture pack—originally created for DuckStation—which completely overhauls the in-game HUD, fonts, weapons icons, and title screens with modern high-resolution fidelity.
  • Caffeine OS has an RTG version of Wipeout included, but even that version with a Pistorm ran incredibly slowly or didn't start at all.

[

UPDATE] - To those of you who keep saying to me there's already a port of Wipeout for the Amiga. " WipEout 2097 was officially ported to the Amiga in 1999 by developer Digital Images and publisher Blittersoft, requiring a PowerPC (PPC) accelerator, a 3D graphics card (supporting Warp3D), 24MB+ Fast RAM, and a CD-ROM drive " So yeh, you need a POWER PC Accelerator. entry.title: Aces of the Pacific - An MS-DOS combat flight sim by Dynamix gets a PC modernization
entry.content:
On this Remembrance Sunday, I thought it would be worth mentioning that the legendary MS-DOS combat flight simulator Aces of the Pacific, has un-officially received a modern PC port. Dubbed Aces of the Pacific: Enhanced, this project was developed by Kylofon through reverse-engineering with the help of AI. While completely revitalizing the classic with upgraded modern performance and improved visuals, the new native version faithfully preserves the magic of Dynamix’s original 1992 masterpiece. For many players, the classic title originally published by Sierra On-Line was the definitive World War II Pacific Theater flight simulator, even outclassing heavyweight contemporary rivals like 1942: Pacific Air War.

▶ Ver vídeo en YouTube

The modernized release allows a new generation of players to dive into the historic aerial conflicts of World War II. True to the original, players can pilot individual single missions or embark on extensive career modes, choosing to fly for the United States Navy, Marines, or Army Air Forces, or take to the skies for the Imperial Japanese Army or Navy. By bridging the gap between the nostalgia of the MS-DOS version and modern PC hardware, Kylofon's project honors the legacy of Dynamix—who famously followed up this landmark simulation with Aces Over Europe in 1993—giving aviation enthusiasts a seamless way to revisit one of the most influential flight games ever made.

Features

  • Smooth 3D view at your display's refresh rate.
  • High resolution (up to 2560 × 1600) with anti-aliasing; optional 16:9 widescreen.
  • Three times the view distance, the finest aircraft and ship models at every distance.
  • Distance haze, a smooth sky and a soft horizon.
  • Held direction keys combine (Left + Down pulls through a turn).
  • Separate flaps down and flaps up keys.
  • A launcher with key bindings.

Requires the CD-ROM version 1.2 of Aces of the Pacific (it includes WWII: 1946). The floppy releases (1.0, 1.01, 1.2 / Patch B and the 1946 expansion disk) don't run: they are separate builds of the game. The launcher and the game say which version a folder holds. A copy is at the Internet Archive: download AcesotP.zip and use the files of its AcesotP\DYNAMIX\AOTP folder.

entry.title: Robocop Arcade - Ranx is working on an Arcade-like version of Robocop for Amiga 500 {AI}

entry.title: ALIENS NEOPLASMA - A brilliant ZX Spectrum game appears on the Amstrad Plus via AI/Devil System
entry.content: The Amstrad CPC Plus has just received a new release with unofficial port of Aliens NeoPlasma, a tense horror platformer developed by Devil System with the help of AI. Originally released to high acclaim on the ZX Spectrum by the Sanchez Crew, this atmospheric title tasks players with guiding protagonist Ashley Smith after she awakens aboard the starship Achilles.
